# FDG3086

> DO NOT use abbreviations or numeric indices for operator overload parameter names.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.7.1 Naming Operator Overload Parameters.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG3086
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Do not use a numeric index in the operator parameter name '{0}'

FDG3086 reports a parameter of an externally visible user-defined operator or conversion operator whose name ends with a digit, such as d1 and d2. A name equal to its type's name apart from case, such as vector3 for Vector3, Vector3? or Vector3[], is not reported. Abbreviations are not checked, because they cannot be told from words. Renaming an operator parameter changes the parameter names in the public API's metadata, which languages that call the operator method by name can use, so the fix is treated as breaking, although C# cannot call an operator with named arguments (CS0571); FDG3086 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
// incorrect parameter naming
public static bool operator ==(DateTimeOffset d1,
                               DateTimeOffset d2);
```
